Claim_Summary: TAS5805M Pin 1 is FAULTz output (Active-LOW)
Verification_Method: Datasheet audit against TI TAS5805M (SLVSEH8B) Pin Functions Table 5-1
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: FAIL: Pin 1 is DGND (Digital Ground). Connecting MCU output creates a dead short to GND. Round 3.1 & 3.2 correctly excised this.

Claim_Summary: TAS5805M Pin 3 is dual-role: Address latch (0x2C) at boot and FAULTz at runtime
Original_Evidence_Source: TI TAS5805M SLVSEH8B Table 7-5, Reg 0x60/0x61, Round 3.2 TAS5805M_PIN3_R12_RESOLUTION.md
Verification_Method: Datasheet register map analysis & web verified TI driver code
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: PASS: Pin 3 latches 0x2C via 4.7kΩ pull-up to DVDD at boot. Reg 0x61=0x0B and 0x60=0x01 enable open-drain FAULTz output.

Claim_Summary: TAS5805M Pin 3 was tied to GND in PCB #0005 schematic but patched on PCB layout with R12
Original_Evidence_Source: sch_netlist_final.json (link_U4 Pin 3) vs pcb_comps.json (link_U4 Pin 3, link_R12)
Verification_Method: Direct JSON netlist parsing of schematic and physical PCB layout
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: PASS: In sch_netlist_final.json Pin 3 is tied to GND. In pcb_comps.json R12 (4.7kΩ) connects Pin 3 to VCC_3V3 (net AMP_ADR).

Claim_Summary: Net AMP_ADR was routed to ESP32 in PCB #0005
Verification_Method: pcb_comps.json net tracing for AMP_ADR
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: FAIL: In pcb_comps.json, net AMP_ADR connects ONLY U4.3 and R12.2. It never connected to any ESP32 GPIO. There was no hardware fault interrupt on #0005.

Claim_Summary: GPIO35 is assigned to Pin 3 FAULTz monitoring (net AMP_FAULTz_ADR)
Verification_Method: ESP32 silicon datasheet TRM (GPIO34-39 GPI characteristics)
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: CONDITIONAL: Conceptually valid (GPI has no internal pullups to disturb boot latch), but currently NC in CAD files. Must not be approved until schematic netlist is edited.

Claim_Summary: GPIO15 strapping pin connected to TAS5805M Pin 12 PDN with 10kΩ pull-up in PCB #0005
Original_Evidence_Source: pcb_comps.json (link_R13, link_U1 Pin 23, link_U4 Pin 12), amplifier_manager.h L6
Verification_Method: Direct netlist inspection of pcb_comps.json and firmware source
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: PASS: In pcb_comps.json, R13 pulls GPIO15/PDN to 3.3V. This forces MTDO HIGH during boot (UART debug log trap) and enables amp prematurely.

Claim_Summary: GPIO13 is assigned to TAS5805M PDN with 10kΩ pull-down to GND
Verification_Method: ESP32 TRM & schematic audit
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: CONDITIONAL: Technically sound (GPIO13 is non-strapping, default weak pull-down), but currently NC in CAD files and firmware still defines PIN_AMP_PDN 15.

Claim_Summary: MP3426 feedback resistors R1=143kΩ, R2=16kΩ produce 12.17V PVDD
Original_Evidence_Source: BOM_PCB1_revB_2026-07-09.csv L16-17 vs MP3426 datasheet Vref=1.225V
Verification_Method: Independent formula verification: Vout = 1.225 * (1 + 143/16)
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: PASS: Vout = 12.173V. Note: early schematic netlist erroneously listed R1=16k, R2=150k (1.35V). BOM revB corrected this.

Claim_Summary: MP3426 switching frequency is 1.22MHz with R9=82kΩ via formula fsw = (100k/R9)*1.0MHz
Verification_Method: MPS MP3426 official datasheet Table 1 & equation RFSET = (860/fsw) - 23
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: FAIL: Fabricated formula! Real MP3426 datasheet Table 1 shows RFSET=82kΩ sets fsw ≈ 510kHz (~0.51MHz). 1.22MHz requires RFSET ≈ 30kΩ.

Claim_Summary: Inductor ripple current is 0.544A at 1.22MHz
Verification_Method: Recalculation using real fsw = 510kHz: dIL = (Vin*D)/(fsw*L)
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: FAIL: Based on fake 1.22MHz. At real fsw = 510kHz, dIL = 1.30A (2.39x larger). Peak current rises to 3.21A under 7.56W load.

Claim_Summary: SWPA6045S-4R7 inductor (Isat=3.6A) has 58.7% saturation margin in normal mode
Verification_Method: Recalculation at 510kHz and elevated temperature (75°C derated Isat=2.88A)
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: FAIL: Saturation margin is severely compromised at 510kHz (peak 1.87A vs 2.88A = 35% margin; under heavy transient peak 3.21A exceeds Isat).

Claim_Summary: Upgrading L1 to SWPA8040S-4R7 (Isat=5.0A) resolves inductor saturation
Original_Evidence_Source: Round 3.2 Target BOM L40, Sunlord datasheet C38117
Verification_Method: Component rating recalculation against 3.21A peak inductor current
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: PASS: SWPA8040S-4R7 has Isat=5.0A, Irms=4.2A. Provides 35.8% margin even under unconstrained peak at 510kHz.

Claim_Summary: C8/C9 0603 10µF MLCCs derate by >70% at 12V DC bias
Verification_Method: Samsung/Murata Class II MLCC DC bias characteristic curves
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: PASS: 0603 10µF 25V X5R retains only 25%~30% capacitance (2.5~3.0µF) at 12V DC bias. Two caps in parallel yield ~5.6µF.

Claim_Summary: Upgrading C8/C9 to 1210 22µF 35V X7R achieves 12.8mV ripple (78% reduction)
Verification_Method: Recalculation with Ceff=26.4µF at REAL fsw=510kHz: dV = (Iout*D)/(fsw*Ceff)
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: FAIL: 12.8mV calculation used erroneous 1.22MHz. At real 510kHz, ripple is ~30.9mV. Still an improvement over 0603 (~74mV), but claim of 12.8mV is false.

Claim_Summary: Bleeder resistor R_BLEED (1.5kΩ 1206) eliminates light-load overshoots above 13.2V
Verification_Method: MP3426 pulse-skipping threshold analysis (minimum on-time ton,min=100ns)
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: UNVERIFIED: 1.5kΩ draws 8.11mA (99mW). Pulse-skipping power threshold is ~300mW at 510kHz. The converter will still skip pulses. Requires bench scope verification.

Claim_Summary: BAT54S Schottky array clamps voice-coil back-EMF within -0.5V to 12.5V
Verification_Method: Nexperia BAT54S datasheet current ratings vs exciter peak current (1.0~1.5A)
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: FAIL: Severe component under-rating! BAT54S is rated IF=200mA continuous, 600mA surge. Exciter inductive kickback carries 1.0~1.5A. BAT54S risks short-circuit destruction.

Claim_Summary: PVDD isolation jumper R_ISO1 (0Ω 2512) safely carries 5.0A
Verification_Method: SMD 2512 jumper specification audit (UNI-ROYAL 25121WJ0000T4E)
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: CONDITIONAL: Standard 2512 0Ω jumpers have max resistance <50mΩ (<20mΩ typ). At 5A, P = I^2*R = 0.5W~1.25W. Must explicitly specify jumper with R < 5mΩ.

Claim_Summary: -3.5dBFS DSP register setting (0x37) is a hardware safety limit
Original_Evidence_Source: Round 3.2 Synthesis Report L72, majn_amplifier_driver.cpp L118-121
Verification_Method: TAS5805M register map audit (Reg 0x4C DIG_VOL is volatile RAM)
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: FAIL: Reg 0x4C is volatile software DSP attenuation. It resets on reboot, crashes, or I2C bus lockup. Calling it 'hardware enforcement clamp' is false.

Claim_Summary: C++ firmware state machine unit tests prove hardware-level safety
Verification_Method: Source code audit of test_firmware_state_machine.cpp (MockHardwareInterface)
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: FAIL: Tests run purely in PC memory against std::map mock objects. Passing unit tests does not validate physical electrical/thermal hardware safety.

Claim_Summary: AAP 50dBA at 30cm is an official statutory infant product safety standard
Verification_Method: Pediatrics 1997 AAP Committee Report vs CPSC 16 CFR Part 1218 / ASTM F2194
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: FAIL: 1997 AAP guidance applies to hospital NICU/nursery ambient noise, not consumer bassinet products. 50dBA is an internal design target, not a statutory standard.

Claim_Summary: Infant micro-vibration limit 0.12g RMS / 18µm displacement is an official safety standard
Verification_Method: Kimura et al. 2017 & ISO 2631-1 audit
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: FAIL: Kimura tested 0.5Hz mechanical rocking (2.4~7.5mm), not 45Hz micro-vibration. ISO 2631-1 covers adult occupational vibration. 0.12g is an internal engineering derivation.

Claim_Summary: IEC 62368-1 Table 38 mandates infant touch surface <= 35.0°C and enclosure <= 40.0°C
Verification_Method: IEC 62368-1 Table 38 (Thermal burn limits for ordinary persons)
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: FAIL: Misquoted standard! IEC 62368-1 TS1 limit for plastic is 60°C. 35°C (mattress) / 40°C (chassis) are internal physiological targets, not IEC 62368-1 clauses.

Claim_Summary: FMEA RPN was reduced by >95% (from 158 down to 7.5) across 12 failure modes
Verification_Method: MAJN_INFANT_SAFETY_FMEA_REGISTER.csv numerical audit
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: FAIL: Subjective paper calculation! RPN reduction was achieved by multiplying lower hypothetical scores on paper without physical fault-injection test evidence.

Claim_Summary: PCB #0006 design input package contains 62-part BOM and complete target netlist
Original_Evidence_Source: Round 3.2 Target BOM CSV (62 parts) vs Target Netlist JSON (15 parts)
Verification_Method: Direct file comparison of PCB0006_BILL_OF_MATERIALS_TARGET.csv vs JSON
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: FAIL: Incomplete netlist! Target JSON contains only 15 components (no capacitors, no sensors, no connectors, no clamp diodes). It is a subsystem snippet, not a full netlist.

Claim_Summary: CI verification suite provides 100% PASS with zero false-pass risk
Verification_Method: Static and dynamic audit of verify_gpio_conflicts.py, verify_power_calculations.py
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: FAIL: verify_gpio_conflicts.py had a header parsing bug auditing pin numbers ('1','2') instead of GPIO names, giving 100% false pass. verify_power skips fault rows.

Claim_Summary: 30-minute auto-cutoff is an enforced KC statutory infant product standard
Original_Evidence_Source: Round 3.2 Track F Report L79, main.cpp L65-68
Verification_Method: KC Child Product Common Safety Standard statutory review
Verified_Finding_Discrepancy: FAIL: KC child product standards do not mandate a 30-minute vibration shutoff. It is an internal protective feature implemented in firmware.
